A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material reorganized from v1’s Appendices A–F into v2’s Appendices A–E.

before.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix E.2 report original synthetic DP-SGD auditing experiments varying the numbers of auditing elements and guesses and the target privacy parameter.

after.justification: Section 6.2 and Appendix D.3 report original DP-SGD auditing experiments. Appendix E.3.2 additionally reports simulations comparing ordinary and adaptive ORA on Count-in-Sets.

M1.justification: The core ORA, maximum-likelihood guessing, and adaptive ORA procedures are retained. Adaptive ORA already appears in v1’s Appendix F, and multiple gradients per dimension already appear in Section 5. The new Count-in-Sets study instantiates these existing ideas; the added DP-SGD pseudocode documents the audited algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds empirical auditing of noiseless binary Count-in-Sets in Appendix E.3.2, whereas v1 treats this algorithm theoretically. The synthetic white-box DP-SGD evaluation remains, without an expansion to real-world datasets.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 8 introduces an empirical comparison between ordinary ORA and adaptive ORA on Count-in-Sets. V1’s empirical comparisons vary configurations of ordinary ORA; its adaptive-versus-ordinary comparisons are theoretical.

E3.justification: The multi-epsilon element-count sweep changes from n = 1000, 2000, 10000, 40000 in v1 Figure 4 to 200, 1000, 4000, 20000 in v2 Figure 7. The new Count-in-Sets experiment fixes 100 sets, varies set size, and uses certainty-only maximum-likelihood guessers with threshold infinity and 95% confidence bounds.

E4.justification: V2 adds a controlled set-size sensitivity study asking how aggregation affects the benefit of adaptive auditing, supported by Figure 8 and Appendix E.3.2. The existing DP-SGD analyses of auditing-element counts and guessing fractions are retained.

E5.justification: Reported repetitions increase from 40 to 100 for the main DP-SGD plots and from 10 to 20 for the multi-epsilon plots. The new Count-in-Sets simulation reports 50 experiments per point. Means and standard errors remain the reporting practice for the main plots.

E6.justification: The empirical record gains adaptive-versus-ordinary ORA results showing increasingly different bounds as Count-in-Sets aggregation grows, plus explicit efficacy curves in Figures 4–5. Retained DP-SGD results also change numerically: at 50 elements per dimension and k = 100, the displayed bound changes from approximately 0.39 in v1 Figure 1 to 0.15 in v2 Figure 2. These are revised experimental reports, not an established cross-version method improvement.

T1.justification: V2 adds average-case distributional privacy definitions, explicit validity/tightness propositions A.14–A.15, and adaptive counting derivations in Appendix E.3.2. It reworks the efficacy–tightness proof through Lemma A.16 and corrects the validity inequality to compare the privacy bound with epsilon(M), rather than p(epsilon(M)). The principal tightness characterizations remain, despite extensive relocation.

C1.justification: The characterization of ORA’s fundamental gaps remains central. V2’s abstract and contribution statement additionally foreground mitigating interference through multiple elements per dimension and adaptivity. These approaches already appear in v1, but their role as claimed main contributions becomes more explicit.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive qualifications about pure versus approximate DP and explicitly limits the experiments to illustrating theoretical insights. It explains how gradient aggregation obstructs auditing without supplying the formal privacy protection supplied by noise and sampling. Applying adaptive ORA comprehensively to DP-SGD is explicitly left for future work.

D1.justification: V2 adds an experiment-code repository link, specifies RDP-based noise calibration and a sampling rate of 0.1, clarifies use of the approximate-DP auditing variant, and supplies DP-SGD pseudocode in Algorithm 3. These improve documentation without independently establishing changes to the underlying retained experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds Kasiviswanathan and Smith on DP semantics and Xiang et al.’s contemporaneous ORA work. The new related-work passage credits Xiang et al. for the interference terminology and distinguishes the papers’ characterization and mitigation contributions. Most research positioning and references remain.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: it creates a Problem Setting section, moves general auditing foundations and the non-abstaining tightness characterization into appendices, and rewrites the contributions and DP-SGD discussion around interference mitigation. The separate conclusion disappears, and explanations throughout the main text and appendices are revised.

P2.justification: V2 adds two empirical-efficacy figures, the Count-in-Sets comparison, and a DP-SGD algorithm display. It swaps and relocates the main experimental figures, replaces their error bars with shaded uncertainty regions, revises legends and captions, moves auditor pseudocode into the appendix, and removes the Markov-chain diagram.

improvement.justification: The reworked efficacy–tightness proof, clearer experimental limitations, reproducibility information, and added adaptive-auditing simulation make v2 easier to assess than v1. However, the new Appendix E.3.2 omits a factor s in ordinary ORA’s expected guess count: it should be s times 2^{-(s-1)}, since a homogeneous set permits s guesses. This exaggerates the quoted advantage at s = 10, although Figure 8 supports the direction of the benefit. The net improvement is therefore limited.
